## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` feature end-to-end. When a `POST /api/owners` request sets `sharesHousehold: true` and another owner already lives at the same household (same last name + address, compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), the create is allowed and every member of that household is given one stable, shared `householdId`, which is then returned via `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

Changes:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `householdId` string to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it and MapStruct maps it automatically.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — Added the persisted `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter.

3. **DB schemas** — Added a `household_id VARCHAR(64)` column to `db/hsqldb/schema.sql` (the test DB, `ddl-auto=none`) and `db/h2/schema.sql`, plus a trailing `NULL` to the column-less seed inserts in `db/hsqldb/data.sql`.

4. **`AssignOwnerHousehold.java`** (new function) — Runs after `BuildOwner`. When `sharesHousehold` is true and a matching household exists, it reuses an existing member's `householdId` or derives a stable one deterministically (first 8 hex chars of `SHA-256(normalizedLastName|normalizedAddress)`), assigns it to the new owner, and back-fills + saves any existing member lacking one so the whole household shares it. It uses the same normalization as `CheckUniqueOwnerHousehold` (which already skips the uniqueness rejection when `sharesHousehold` is true). No match / flag unset ⇒ no id assigned.

5. **`owners.POST.yml`** — Wired the `assignHousehold` step into the transactional pipeline between `build` and `defaultRegistrationDate`.

The deterministic derivation guarantees independent joiners compute the same id even before the existing member's saved value is visible, so the shared identifier is stable regardless of ordering.
